title: Air India to Shift More Europe, US Flights to Mumbai, Eyes Bengaluru as Third Hub
excerpt: CEO Tewolde Gebremariam said Pakistan's airspace closure hits Delhi harder than Mumbai, so westbound growth will move to Mumbai, eastern growth will stay in Delhi, and Bengaluru is being explored as a third hub.
body:
• Air India will shift a larger share of its Europe- and America-bound services to Mumbai because the closure of Pakistan's airspace affects Delhi more than Mumbai, CEO and Managing Director Tewolde Gebremariam said on November 3.
  • Delhi remains an important hub: Europe and America flights will continue from the capital, and eastern and south-eastern network growth will be centred on Delhi.
  • The airline is actively exploring Bengaluru as a third hub, and will rebalance its network and look for more wide-body aircraft, PTI reported.
  • For travellers: this is a network direction, not a schedule change — no specific route moves, dates or booking changes were announced.

Air India is looking to rebalance its international operations by shifting a larger share of its Europe- and America-bound services to Mumbai, its CEO and Managing Director Tewolde Gebremariam said at the Aviation India and South Asia 2026 conference on Tuesday, November 3. The reason is operational: the ongoing closure of Pakistani airspace to Indian carriers has hit Delhi harder than Mumbai, prompting the airline to reconsider how it deploys its long-haul network, ANI reported.

"We will continue to have Europe and America flights from Delhi, but more will be moving to Mumbai."

— Tewolde Gebremariam, Air India CEO and Managing Director

What moves, and what stays

Gebremariam was explicit that Delhi is not being downgraded. Delhi will continue to have Europe and America flights, while growth on the eastern and south-eastern sides of the network — routes not affected by the airspace closure — will be centred on Delhi by and large, he said, according to ANI. The rebalance is about where new westbound capacity goes, not about withdrawing the capital's existing long-haul services. PTI reported the same plan in parallel: the overseas network will be rebalanced, costs reduced, and more wide-body aircraft sought.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Ddq1b_olEl5/

Bengaluru as a possible third hub

The airline is also actively exploring Bengaluru as a third potential operational hub, alongside Delhi and Mumbai. "We are also exploring Bangalore as a third hub, because this is a huge country," Gebremariam said. He added that the airline is improving its international sales force and international points of sale to rebalance against India points of sale, which would also help mitigate currency fluctuation. No timetable or route list for a Bengaluru hub was announced.

The headwinds behind the move

Gebremariam put the airspace problem alongside industry-wide pressures. Fuel prices are, in his words, more than double last year's for every carrier, and Middle East geopolitics affect all airlines directly or indirectly — but the Pakistan airspace closure is, he said, a unique problem for Air India that its competitors do not face in the same way. He described the pressures as short-term headwinds the airline needs to navigate to emerge stronger for long-term growth. For diaspora travellers, the practical effect to watch is scheduling: westbound flights routed from Mumbai avoid the longest detours, which is why future Europe and US capacity growth is being pointed there first.

nri_angle: For US- and Europe-based NRIs, the rebalance means more long-haul choice from Mumbai over time and a possible Bengaluru long-haul hub — but no route has been announced or moved yet, so existing bookings are unaffected by this statement alone.
